sources.title: Cellular energetics lecture.pdf
sources.text: ATP hydrolysis releases free energy when ATP reacts with water to form ADP and inorganic phosphate. Cells couple this favorable reaction to processes that require energy. ATP is regenerated from ADP and phosphate using energy from other reactions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains what ATP hydrolysis does in cells?
choices: It releases free energy that cells can couple to energy-requiring processes.
It stores energy by converting ADP and phosphate into ATP without any input.
It directly powers all cell work without needing other reactions.
hints: Look for the choice about energy release, not energy storage.
The source says cells couple ATP hydrolysis to energy-requiring processes.
questions.workedExample: A cell needs energy to move a molecule across a membrane. ATP hydrolysis can provide the released free energy that is coupled to that transport.

questions.prompt: If ATP is used in a cell, what must happen to keep the ATP supply available?
hints: Think about what the source says happens after ATP is used.
What molecules are combined to remake ATP? What provides the energy?
